text: Every admiral in the navy has an Arabic title... they just don't know it.
Ameer. A commander: the one who gives the orders.
In Norman Sicily, in the 1100s, the king's top commander ran his fleet... and his title was Arabic: amir of amirs.
Latin wrote it ammiratus... French made it amiral... and English slipped in a D, from admire. Admiral.
Your turn. Its root means to command. This is from surah Yaseen: amruhu. His ship, his army, or his command?
إِنَّما أَمْرُهُ إِذا أَرادَ شَيْئًا أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ
COMMAND! When He wills a thing, His command is only: Be... and it is.
So who's the real amir of your house? Comment it!
